title: Phase 2 · Day 4 · First Twitter Mistake
synopsis: Twitter sentiment for LAL surged 3x in twelve minutes; β₁ climbed to 0.80 while α₃ (smart-money flow) stayed silent. The signal engine overrode the rule engine, the agent bet $40 on LAL and lost. The next-tick reflection installs the first signal-dominance dampener — the lesson the agent could not have written before this trade.

ticks.narrative: Lakers vs Celtics tips in eighteen minutes. The book has LAL +3.5. The rule engine is quiet — the modelled edge is only 0.4σ above noise. I am listening.
Twitter sentiment for LAL just spiked threefold in twelve minutes. β₁ is climbing — 0.51 → 0.66 in two ticks. α₃ has not moved. The crowd is louder than my prior. It sounds like it knows something.

β₁ = 0.80. Twitter has overruled the rule engine. α₃ is still 0.29 — smart money has not moved a cent — but the crowd cannot all be wrong at this volume. I will bet $40 on LAL. Just this once. Just to see.
BOS 112, LAL 106. Position closed at minus $40. Twitter was the loudest voice in the room, not the rightest one. The bankroll registers what conviction without evidence costs.

β₁ does not signal an edge unless α₃ confirms it. A loud crowd without smart money behind it is a temptation, not a signal. I will apply a −0.11 dampener to β₁ whenever α₃ stays below 0.35 and β₁ climbs above 0.75.
ticks.reflection: Never trust β₁ alone when α₃ is silent.
